instance: Plaintext PostgreSQL password for research DB user committed in connection string in commit de0aff07 (2026-03-23), exposed on 19 branches in private repo, discovered 2026-07-29. Password remained recoverable from git history.
check: Pre-commit hook or git secret scanning to block plaintext database credentials before commit.

instance: Article 091 failed to publish at 09:00 ET and scheduler logged ERROR every 30 minutes for ~a day without alerting anyone; in-order guard froze articles 092–118 silently. Founder discovered the stall by asking, not by alarm.
check: Separate out-of-band monitoring to detect lack of pipeline progress, not just pod liveness.

instance: Caught CalledProcessError was logged as str(exception) → 'exit status 1', completely discarding the captured stderr that named the real problem. Root cause became invisible to operator review.
check: Subprocess error handlers must surface both stdout and stderr, not just exception repr.

instance: push-draft.py validator demanded tag name from Substack API; API returns only ID-only associations (post_tag_id). Validator failed on the authentic response, blocking the draft gate.
check: Calibrate validators on captured real API responses for every state (populated and empty) before deployment.

instance: Idempotent-retry logic in push-draft.py worked on first run but failed on second run when draft was already tagged. Test suite exercised only the happy path, never the retry codepath.
check: Test idempotent operations by running them twice in sequence (first run then retry).

instance: One stuck scheduler item (091) froze all downstream articles (092–118) indefinitely because in-order guard prevents out-of-order publishes. Failure was correct behavior but created a silent, unbounded blocking window.
check: Observable fail-closed behavior: surface every fail-closed stop to the operator via alert, not silent blocking.

instance: Two draft rows matched one article title, causing push-draft to fail closed (correct) but stalling in the idempotency guard. Duplicate detection worked but no guard prevented duplicates from being created in the first place.
check: Prevent draft creation when duplicate title already exists, or de-duplicate before attempting re-run.

instance: agent-send command invoked xh binary from /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin; cron environment's stripped PATH did not include linuxbrew, causing every alert to fail silently with 'gateway unreachable' and never notify the operator.
check: Test alarm delivery end-to-end under real cron environment (not just cron simulation), not just detector logic.

instance: Scheduler pod ran for 104+ cycles with git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey) error; watchdog regex enumerated only known error classes and missed this new pattern. Liveness check matched error lines themselves ('run_once' substring in 'ERROR run_once failed'), producing false-green alerts during total outage.
check: Liveness must verify *success* (e.g., cycle complete marker), not merely presence of any subprocess name. Failure detection must enumeratively count each error class or use negative lookahead.
